pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks the seeded rows are all 0.
'AC-2' test asserts '★ Second item' with the other items unmarked; src/index.js item().
'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and expects only those, in id order, with status 200.
'AC-4' checks both '/' and '/?show=all' return all three items in id order.
'AC-5' checks the exact link markup on both views.
'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for 'Starred', 'none', empty and '__proto__'. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'; 'AC-7' test asserts it. The traffic Worker passes the path to the app unchanged.

findings.what: The migration adds a CHECK (starred IN (0,1)) constraint. The spec asks only for a flag. It is harmless but not asked for, and the AC-1 test asserts it.
findings.fix: Keep it and note it in the PR, or drop the constraint and the assertion.

findings.what: The README mentions only ?show=starred. It omits show=all, the 400 on other values, the ★ marker and the navigation links.
findings.fix: Add one line covering show=all, the 400 response and the ★ marker.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and both decisions: starred items keep id order, and the view is a GET query parameter.
All 7 acceptance items are named by tests. All 4 state-table rows have tests that check the list, the message and the link. The spec was added in the same commit as the code, and its go is dated.
The tests assert rendered behaviour and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them; CI is declared to run them. The traffic fake-app change is a needed adaptation, not a loosening.
The README is updated but thin (low finding).
The query parsing is correct. Object.hasOwn guards prototype keys, and the SQL is static (the WHERE comes from a fixed map).
Titles are still escaped. show is validated against a whitelist and never reaches SQL. No injection path found.
Only minimal server-rendered HTML changed; the diff has no CSS or UI component files.
No UI files are in the diff and no browser is available.
The title is under 72 characters. The claims are true of the diff, including the loosened route regex in traffic-config-check.mjs, which the PR discloses.
